column1: # package-sizes-windows.tsv: measured seconds for `go test -short` on
# windows-latest, the hosted image the test-windows-pr leg runs on. Its sibling
# package-sizes.tsv records the idle-LINUX size and is a different measurement;
# the two are kept apart because neither predicts the other. cmd/nova-bus is
# 6.4 s on idle Linux and at least 100 s here; cmd/nova-swarm is 51.0 s there
# and 37.0 s here. The difference is processes: the git-fixture packages spawn
# one per case and Windows pays the most per process, while nova-swarm's heavy
# cases are gated behind testing.Short() and skip on this leg. A multiplier over
# the Linux column would be wrong in both directions, which is why these numbers
# are measured and checked in rather than derived.
# CENSORED ROWS. 100.0 and 100.1 are not sizes, they are the 100 s per-package
# timeout the leg carried when it took the measurement: the true size of those
# four is AT LEAST that and is not known. The shard planner treats a row at or
# over the shard budget as "shard it", so a censored row lands on the right side
# of the decision without pretending to a precision it does not have. Replace a
# censored row with a real number when a leg with a larger ceiling measures one.
# Measured on run of PR #1332 (integration-4), 2026-09-18, windows-latest,
# `go test -short -count=1 -timeout 100s`.
